key_insight: QESChunker unifies overlapping and non-overlapping RAG chunking under a question–evidence utility objective for supervised, budget-aware index construction.
engineering_relevance: It offers a principled alternative to heuristic chunking for improving complete-evidence retrieval with a fixed retriever.
method: Build document-specific static indices using human-annotated or LLM-generated question–evidence pairs, without held-out test queries.
Optimize non-overlapping chunks exactly in polynomial time using dynamic programming.
Optimize overlapping chunks with a greedy algorithm offering a (1−1/√e) approximation guarantee for the monotone submodular objective.
evidence_signal: Across two self-constructed and three public datasets, both variants outperform existing chunkers in complete-evidence recall in nearly all evaluated settings under matched overlap regimes and a fixed hybrid retriever.
watch_item: Deployment requires question–evidence supervision; annotation cost and LLM-generated evidence quality warrant validation.
paper_title: QESChunker: A Single Objective Unifies Overlapping and Non-Overlapping Chunking for RAG
